Stanford Court: $99 security deposit when you lease by Apr 13, 2026

Redfin 'LOWERED FEES' flags across Irvine Co listings (Spectrum, 92620)

renewal_note: Anecdotal (TalkIrvine forum, mostly undated/older; one r/irvine mirror post, undated): renewal offers of ~6.7% (tenant offset by negotiating a 10-month lease), attempts at 7%+ negotiated to ~4%, a ~9% renewal increase question on r/irvine with no outcome shown, and one tenant told Irvine Co would not lower a $2,260 2BR renewal. Month-to-month reportedly quoted at rent + 30% (one TalkIrvine post).
negotiation_note: Forum advice (anecdotal): compare your renewal quote to current listed prices for vacant comparable units and ask for the new-resident price; lease length is negotiable (16->12, 10-month leases mentioned); leverage mostly comes from being genuinely ready to move. Irvine Co specials are typically reduced security deposits ($99 / reduced deposit 'when you lease by <date>') and lowered fees rather than weeks free; the only large free-rent example found is up to 6 weeks free at The Enclave (Costa Mesa) on 14+ month leases, c. 2008 lease-up (OCBJ, date inferred).
evidence: Recurring pattern: rolling 'reduced/$99 security deposit when you lease by <date>' offers that are renewed with new deadlines every few months (Dec 2025, Apr 2026, Jul/Aug 2026), plus 'lowered fees' tags; free-rent weeks are rare (only lease-up example found is c. 2008). Could NOT confirm from any source that Irvine Co uses daily pricing or a specific revenue-management system, nor how its lease-term pricing is structured; searches for its site disclaimers returned nothing. Industry context: Yardi Revenue IQ docs say longer leases are often priced lower and prices depend on move-in date and lease length (general, not Irvine-specific). No source tied Irvine Co to the RealPage litigation.
